title: Which prompt carries the context?
scenario: You are sending a reply to a client who has been waiting a week for an answer about their refund.
task: Which prompt is more likely to produce a send-ready draft?
promptA: Rewrite this email in a more professional style.
promptB: Rewrite the draft below as a reply to a client who has waited a week for a refund decision: apologetic but confident. Keep every commitment we made. Maximum five sentences.

feedback.a: “Professional” points at a generic register — the model has no idea who is reading or why. Expect stiff boilerplate that fixes the tone and misses the situation.
feedback.b: Audience, situation, tone, boundary and length in one breath. The draft can now land on the first try — or fail in ways you can name and correct.

hints: Which prompt tells the model something it could not possibly know?
explanation: Context sentences are the cheapest quality upgrade in prompting: audience, purpose, knowns and material rewiring every prediction that follows. The client is not in the draft — supply her, and the draft transforms.
